articles.title: Intel confirms Crescent Island GPU will pack 32 Xe3P cores and up to 480GB of memory
articles.text:
The big picture: Intel announced its Crescent Island data center GPU last year before sharing more details at Computex 2026 in June. The company has now revealed all the key specifications, including core count, cache, memory, and more. Team Blue also emphasized that Crescent Island is optimized for performance per watt and improved AI model support rather than raw compute performance.
At the Hot Chips 2026 symposium in Palo Alto this week, Intel revealed that Crescent Island will feature 32 Xe3P cores, 256 XMX engines, 32MB of unified L2 cache, a PCIe Gen5 x16 interface, and a 350W TDP for the air-cooled model. Intel will ship Crescent Island accelerators with 160GB of LPDDR5X memory, but the chip will support ODM designs with up to 480GB of VRAM.
Xe3P offers a marked improvement over both Xe2 and Xe3 in terms of AI capabilities. The XMX units in the new architecture have a 16-deep systolic array, compared with the four-deep design used in their predecessors. The new Xe Vector Engine also gains support for FP8 and FP4 precision, as well as microscaling formats, while doubling the GRF to 1MB per Xe core.
Other notable changes include a more capable memory subsystem, packing 512KB of L1 cache/SLM memory per Xe core, as well as full-rate FP64 support with 64 FMAs per Xe core. Intel also noted that the new architecture comes with an industry-standard AI software stack that is open, upstreamed, and Day 0-ready for Crescent Island.
Crescent Island is specifically designed for agentic AI rather than gaming, so it does not include any 3D or ray-tracing hardware found in Intel's consumer graphics chips. Instead, Team Blue has used the freed-up space to pack eight Vector Engines and eight XMX Engines into each Xe3P core, for a total of 256 of each in the full GPU.
The Xe3P graphics architecture is an AI-focused variant of the standard Xe3 architecture used in Core Ultra 300-series "Panther Lake" chips for laptops and compact desktops. Xe3P is also expected to power Intel's Arc-C series GPUs for client devices. Customer sampling for Crescent Island is expected to begin in the current quarter, with the official launch slated for 2027.

articles.title: Preserving glow-in-the-dark art and fashion for future generations
articles.text:
Fashionistas of a certain age no doubt remember the late designer Stephen Sprouse, who gave Blondie’s Debbie Harry her distinctive Bowery punk style. Sprouse’s first collections in the mid-1980s made a major splash, melding graffiti prints, a playful ’60s aesthetic, and bright Day-Glo colors that won admirers such as Andy Warhol.
Several examples of Sprouse’s work are preserved in the textiles collection of the Indianapolis Museum of Art at Newfields, where conservationists are trying to learn more about the phosphorescent and fluorescent pigments the designer used in his creations in order to keep the colors from dulling over time. They described recent advances in that research at a meeting of the American Chemical Society (ACS) held this week in Chicago.
Scientists began describing minerals that glowed in the dark as phosphors in the Middle Ages. Typically, such materials take on a charge when exposed to light, storing the absorbed energy and releasing it gradually as re-emitted light. Henri Becquerel discovered radioactive decay in 1896 because of his work with phosphorescent uranium salts: He left the salts in a closed drawer with photographic plates, which fogged up even without a light source. DayGlo paints and similar materials exploit the related phenomenon of fluorescence. DayGlo pigments fluoresce in daylight by essentially converting UV light into visible light to produce brighter, more vibrant colors.
Sprouse is not the only one to find inspiration in DayGlo and similar phosphorescent and fluorescent materials. All glow-in-the-dark toys, stickers, paint, coatings in fluorescent lamps, cathode-ray tube TVs, and some clock dials rely on phosphorescence. (By contrast, glow sticks rely on a chemiluminescent process.) They’re also commonly used for traffic signage and on safety gear.
DayGlo pigments were used extensively during World War II to make fluorescent fabric panels for US ground troops, while DayGlo’s black light paints were used on Navy aircraft carriers to enable planes to land at night. Artists have used both phosphorescent and fluorescence materials extensively from the mid-20th century on, most notably for psychedelic art and Sprouse’s designs.

articles.title: 'We are not afraid to call evil evil' — Metro 2039 creative director discusses how the Russia-Ukraine war has impacted the game and its story in which there are 'no gray zones'
articles.text:
Metro 2039 creative director shares how the Russia-Ukraine war has affected the game, says there are 'no gray zones' in the story and 'we are not afraid to call evil evil'
The initial plans for the upcoming Metro game were changed as a result of the conflict
- Metro 2039 creative director Andriy Shevchenko discusses how the Russia-Ukraine war has impacted the game
- The developer says, "We are not afraid to call evil evil"
- He adds that there are "no gray zones" in the story
Metro 2039 creative director Andriy Shevchenko has shared how the events of the Russia-Ukraine war have manifested in the upcoming first-person shooter.
The next installment in the Metro series was revealed earlier this year and is expected to deliver another dark survival story set in the heart of the Moscow metro, where the last survivors of the nuclear apocalypse struggle to exist.
At the time, Bloch explained that the team at Ukrainian studio 4A Games had everything planned for the next chapter, until it all changed in 2020, and "more significantly in 2022" with Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
As a result, the studio "changed the story to be even more about choices, actions, consequences, and what you have to pay to have a future."
"Now war is our reality, and our message has shifted to be about the circumstance, the cost of silence, the horrors of tyranny, and the price of freedom," Shevchenko said.
Now, in a new interview with TechRadar Gaming alongside executive producer Jon Bloch, the developers explained how the real-life impact of the ongoing war has influenced the game's messaging and the story's moral core.
"We are not afraid to call evil evil," Shevchenko said. "If you see evil, we now have a protagonist [The Stranger] who can talk, who can share his own thoughts. He will call this character, this situation, this story element evil. It is bad. And there are no gray zones."

"But who is your enemy?" he teased.

articles.title: Evadir la cámara puede salvarte de caer en una estafa sentimental digital
articles.text:
Evitar las videollamadas al iniciar una relación en línea puede ser más que una simple preferencia: en muchos casos, constituye una señal de advertencia sobre posibles estafas románticas. Según datos de Kaspersky, uno de cada cinco usuarios comenzó a sospechar de un fraude cuando su interlocutor se negó de manera reiterada a mostrarse en video, mientras que la mitad de quienes fueron objetivo de estafadores se toparon con perfiles falsos, una táctica conocida como catfishing.
Las consecuencias, lejos de limitarse a una decepción sentimental, pueden derivar en pérdidas económicas o en el robo de identidad, por lo que resulta fundamental identificar a tiempo ciertos patrones de comportamiento.
PUBLICIDAD
Cuáles son las señales de estafa en aplicaciones de citas
Las plataformas de citas en línea han facilitado nuevas formas de socializar, pero también han abierto la puerta a delitos como el catfishing y las estafas amorosas. Uno de los primeros indicadores de riesgo es la negativa persistente a realizar videollamadas.
Kaspersky reporta que el 21 % de los usuarios que identificaron un intento de estafa notaron esta conducta antes de otras señales. La imposibilidad de comprobar la identidad real de la persona tras el perfil es un recurso frecuente para quienes buscan engañar.
PUBLICIDAD
Otra práctica habitual consiste en acelerar el vínculo emocional y, tras ganarse la confianza, solicitar ayuda económica bajo pretextos variados: emergencias médicas, problemas familiares o gastos de viaje. El 40 % de las víctimas terminó enviando dinero, mientras que el 29 % sufrió robo de identidad.
De acuerdo con los expertos, el traslado de la conversación fuera de la plataforma, el envío de enlaces sospechosos y las solicitudes de información personal también son comportamientos que deben alertar al usuario.
PUBLICIDAD
“En las estafas románticas, el delincuente necesita construir confianza antes de intentar obtener dinero o información de la víctima. Por eso, puede mantener conversaciones durante días o semanas, mostrar interés constante y crear una historia creíble, pero evitar situaciones que permitan comprobar quién está realmente detrás del perfil”, señala Fabiano Tricarico, Director de Productos para el Consumidor para América Latina en Kaspersky.
“Negarse repetidamente a realizar una videollamada, buscar excusas para no encontrarse o comenzar a solicitar ayuda económica son señales que no deberían ignorarse. Antes de confiar en alguien que solo conocemos en línea, es importante verificar su identidad y nunca permitir que la conexión emocional reemplace las precauciones de seguridad”, agrega el especialista.
PUBLICIDAD
Recomendaciones para protegerse de estafas románticas en línea
Frente al auge de engaños en entornos virtuales, los especialistas sugieren adoptar una serie de precauciones para evitar caer en fraudes. La primera recomendación es prestar atención a quienes evitan de forma reiterada las videollamadas.
Si bien existen motivos legítimos para rechazar una llamada puntual, la negativa constante, especialmente tras varias conversaciones, debe ser motivo de desconfianza. Las videollamadas permiten confirmar que la imagen y la identidad corresponden realmente a la persona del perfil.
PUBLICIDAD
También es esencial evitar compartir información sensible en las etapas iniciales de la interacción. Datos como dirección, lugar de trabajo, rutinas, documentos o información financiera pueden ser utilizados para suplantación de identidad o fraudes adicionales.
La rapidez con la que se desarrolla la relación y la aparición de solicitudes de dinero deben considerarse señales de alerta. Los estafadores suelen crear una historia convincente y buscan generar un vínculo emocional intenso en poco tiempo, para luego inventar emergencias que justifiquen la petición de ayuda económica.
PUBLICIDAD
Otra medida clave consiste en desconfiar de los enlaces y archivos enviados por un match reciente. Estos pueden dirigir a páginas de phishing o instalar software malicioso con el objetivo de robar datos personales. La verificación de la procedencia de cualquier enlace resulta fundamental antes de abrirlo.
Cómo reforzar la seguridad de cuentas ante fraudes amorosos
Más allá de la prudencia en las conversaciones, la protección de la información digital es fundamental. Entre las recomendaciones técnicas figura el uso de contraseñas distintas para cada servicio, la activación de la autenticación en dos pasos y la actualización regular del sistema operativo y las aplicaciones.
PUBLICIDAD
Detectar comportamientos sospechosos y proteger los datos personales son pasos clave para evitar que una interacción casual en línea termine en pérdidas económicas o en la exposición de información sensible a delincuentes.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Ce satellite va assister à sa propre mort et tout enregistrer
articles.text:
L’Agence spatiale européenne prépare, pour 2027, le lancement de Draco, un satellite construit pour se désintégrer sous ses propres capteurs. L’engin embarquera 200 capteurs et quatre caméras pour filmer sa propre rentrée atmosphérique, et une capsule transmettra ensuite les données recueillies vers le sol.
Prononcez Draco, mais comprenez Destructive Re-entry Assessment Container Object. Vous vous souvenez peut-être de cette espèce de cube développé par l’Agence spatiale européenne (ESA) et l’entreprise espagnole Deimos, sous un contrat de 3 millions d’euros pour la phase de démarrage.
L'’engin pèse entre 150 et 200 kg, fait la taille d’une machine à laver selon l’ESA et volera moins de douze heures avant sa rentrée atmosphérique complète, le temps que ses 200 capteurs et ses quatre caméras mesurent en temps réel la température, la dégradation des matériaux et les émissions de gaz à chaque altitude. Une capsule de 40 cm, conçue pour résister à la chaleur, conservera ces données et les transmettra vers un satellite géostationnaire pendant sa descente en parachute, avant l'’amerrissage.
Draco appartient au programme Space Safety de l’ESA, dont la charte « Zero Debris » a pour objectif d’arrêter, d’ici 2030, toute création de nouveaux débris en orbite.
Le bouclier thermique en liège portugais et feutres ablatifs
Une fois la capsule séparée du reste du satellite, la géométrie de l’engin devra stabiliser sa chute sans tournoiement incontrôlé, à partir de trois configurations déjà éprouvées.
La capsule déploiera ensuite un parachute vers 10 km d’altitude et disposera d'une fenêtre de 20 minutes pour transmettre entre 20 Mo et 1 Go de données à un satellite géostationnaire avant l’amerrissage, tandis que des marqueurs verts, fournis par l’entreprise espagnole Astros Solutions, seront visibles depuis le sol et depuis les airs, pendant une campagne d’observation externe destinée à recouper les mesures internes.
Les ingénieurs prévoient aussi un essai final du parachute depuis 25 km d’altitude, largué par ballon, pendant que la construction du satellite se poursuit jusqu’à la fin de l’année.
Une fusée chinoise de 25 tonnes est déjà retombée trois fois sans contrôle
Le 30 juillet 2022, un étage de la fusée chinoise Longue Marche 5B, d’une masse de 25 tonnes, a effectué une rentrée atmosphérique sans aucun contrôle, avant de s’abîmer dans l’océan Indien, au large des Philippines. Cette chute était la troisième du genre pour ce type de lanceur, après des débris tombés en Côte d’Ivoire en mai 2020 et une désintégration au-dessus de la péninsule arabique en avril 2021. Contrairement à la plupart des lanceurs, le corps de la fusée chinoise atteint l’orbite avec sa charge utile, sans dispositif de désorbitation contrôlée.
Les données de Draco doivent nourrir le « design-for-demise », une méthode de conception poussant les fabricants à choisir des matériaux capables de brûler entièrement en altitude, plutôt que de retomber en un seul morceau imprévisible.
Depuis 1957, environ 8 836 satellites ont été envoyés en orbite et 5 362 restent aujourd’hui en service, selon l’Office des Nations unies pour les affaires spatiales (UNOOSA). L’Agence spatiale européenne recense, de surcroît, plus de 34 000 objets de plus de 10 cm et plus de 128 millions de fragments de moins d’un centimètre en orbite, avec plus de 500 événements de fragmentation à l’origine de la majorité de ces débris et plus de 13 000 rapprochements dangereux dénombrés chaque semaine entre satellites actifs et débris.
Les futures constellations de SpaceX, OneWeb, Amazon et Telesat pourraient, selon des projections qu’on vous a relayées, multiplier cette population par trois à cinq dans les prochaines années.

articles.title: The Gilded Age (HBO Max) : un teaser opulent et une date de sortie pour la saison 4
articles.text:
The Gilded Age (HBO Max) : un teaser opulent et une date de sortie pour la saison 4
La série du créateur de Downton Abbey prépare son retour sur le service de streaming HBO Max avec une quatrième saison qui se dévoile à travers un premier teaser.
Julian Fellowes a encore des histoires à raconter sur l'âge doré de l'élite New Yorkaise dans la quatrième saison de The Gilded Age. La série du créateur de Downton Abbey se prépare en effet à revenir sur HBO Max en novembre prochain et son premier teaser montre qu'obtenir ce que l'on veut n'est pas sans risque.
Rendez-vous en novembre
Huit nouveaux épisodes de The Gilded Age arriveront sur le service de streaming HBO Max dès le lundi 2 novembre prochain, diffusés à raison d'un nouvel épisode par semaine.
Dans cette saison 4 de la série nommée aux Emmy Awards, "Bertha Russell (Carrie Coon) a bouleversé l'ordre établi de la haute société, mais son ascension fulgurante n'est pas sans conséquences pour les siens, alors qu'Agnes van Rhijn (Christine Baranski) est bien décidée à reprendre la place qui lui revient," indique le synopsis officel.
"Tandis que Marian (Louisa Jacobson) forge son propre destin et que Peggy (Denée Benton) cherche à se faire accepter par sa future belle-famille, tous vont apprendre qu'en cette nouvelle ère, il faut parfois se méfier de ce que l'on souhaite…"
La longue distribution de la série compte également toujours sur les talents de Cynthia Nixon, Morgan Spector, Taissa Farmiga, Harry Richardson, Jordan Donica ou encore Blake Ritson.
Cette saison 4 ajoute aussi de nouvelles têtes au casting dont Taylor Trensch, James Scully, Dennis Haysbert, Maggie Kuntz, Neal Huff, Bonnie Milligan, Jim Gaffigan, Dallas Roberts, Andrew Burnap, Elizabeth Marvel et Adrienne Warren.

The Gilded Age revient sur HBO Max dès le 2 novembre 2026.

articles.title: iPhone 17 Pro (256 GB) chega a um dos menores preços recentes • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
iPhone 17 Pro (256 GB) chega a um dos menores preços recentes
iPhone 17 Pro (256 GB) tem câmeras de 48 MP e tela OLED de 120 Hz; celular da Apple atinge um dos menores preços dos últimos meses com desconto de 30% no Pix
O iPhone 17 Pro de 256 GB está saindo por R$ 8.048 no Pix no Mercado Livre. O celular da Apple com câmeras de 48 MP, tela OLED de 120 Hz e chip A19 Pro continua caro, mas alcança um dos menores preços vistos nos últimos meses com desconto de 30% sobre o preço original de R$ 11.499.
O kit de câmeras do iPhone 17 Pro inclui uma wide com OIS e uma ultrawide, que capturam belas cenas em ambientes abertos, e uma telefoto com zoom óptico de 4x para aproximações com ganho de detalhes, todas de 48 MP. A frontal Center Stage de 18 MP tira selfies na horizontal mesmo com o celular em pé.
Seu chip A19 Pro e os 12 GB de RAM suportam apps pesados em multitarefa, games exigentes e soluções do Apple Intelligence localmente. Segundo a maçã, o celular é 40% mais poderoso que concorrentes diretos. Os 256 GB de armazenamento disponibilizam espaço adequado para guardar fotos e vídeos.
Seu corpo de alumínio recebe o vidro Ceramic Shield de ambos os lados, resistente contra acidentes cotidianos. A certificação IP68 adiciona proteção em cenários como ambientes com muita poeira e mergulhos acidentais.
A tela Super Retina XDR OLED de 6,3″ do iPhone 17 Pro conta com ProMotion de 120 Hz e brilho de até 3.000 nits, combinação que a torna capaz de reproduzir imagens com cores autênticas e com alta fluidez nas transições em apps e games, além de garantir a visibilidade em qualquer lugar.
Sua bateria resiste a 31 horas de reprodução de vídeo segundo a Apple, suporta MagSafe e é capaz de injetar uma carga de 50% em 20 minutos via USB-C. Assim, o celular permite uso prolongado mesmo quando longe de tomadas e carregadores.
O iPhone 17 Pro de 256 GB (R$ 8.048 no Pix) conversa com redes 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6.0 e NFC. O celular da Apple roda iOS 26 e é elegível a pelo menos cinco atualizações do sistema operacional.
Aviso de ética: ao clicar em um link de afiliado, o preço não muda para você e recebemos uma comissão.

articles.title: Apple Introduces M6 and M5 Ultra Processors Series
articles.text:
Tuesday, August 25th 2026
	
		
	
	
	
Apple Introduces M6 and M5 Ultra Processors Series
Apple today debuted M6 in the new Mac mini and M5 Ultra in the new Mac Studio, providing an extraordinary leap in performance and AI capabilities. M6, Apple's first state-of-the-art 2-nanometer chip, advances every compute block, delivering gains across every dimension of performance. The chip features a larger 12-core CPU complex with the world's fastest CPU core, a larger 12-core GPU with Neural Accelerators, a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and up to 170 GB/s of unified memory bandwidth.
M5 Ultra, the ultimate powerhouse for pro and AI workloads, uses next-generation UltraFusion technology to form a quad-die architecture for the first time in an M-series system on a chip (SoC). The chip includes an up-to-36-core CPU and up-to-80-core GPU with a massive 1.2 TB/s of unified memory bandwidth, 50 percent more than M3 Ultra. With their advanced technologies, these SoCs deliver extraordinary compute with industry-leading power efficiency, empowering users to do even more on a desktop.
"Today, we're debuting the next giant leap in performance and AI compute for Apple silicon with the incredibly advanced M6 and the most powerful M-series chip yet, M5 Ultra," said Sri Santhanam, Apple's vice president of Silicon Engineering Group. "Built using the cutting-edge 2 nm process, M6 combines a new CPU complex, two additional CPU and GPU cores, a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and more unified memory bandwidth to power through workloads with amazing energy efficiency. And for the ultimate desktop performance and the ability to run massive AI models, M5 Ultra features a massive GPU, now with Neural Accelerators, and more unified memory bandwidth, pushing the boundaries of what a desktop can do."
M6: Optimized Design and Enhanced Performance
Designed to power the workflows of everyday users, students, developers, AI hobbyists, and enterprises, M6 offers the ideal balance of performance, power efficiency, and on-device AI to effortlessly fly through daily tasks, coding, and creative projects.
M6 is built using cutting-edge 2 nm process technology, packing greater transistor density into a smaller die for a major leap in performance and power efficiency. M6 also introduces a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, providing up to 2x the peak compute over previous generations to make on-device AI workflows run even faster. System frameworks can automatically utilize both engines simultaneously, enabling applications to see faster model execution.
M6 has a brand-new 12-core CPU complex—two more cores than M5—that consists of 2 super cores, 4 performance cores, and 6 efficiency cores. It delivers the world's fastest single-threaded performance and up to 1.2x faster multithreaded performance as compared to M5, and up to 2.4x faster than M1. The super cores blaze through single-threaded workloads, the performance cores use less power and join the super cores to run demanding multithreaded workloads, and the efficiency cores handle everyday background tasks—all with industry-leading performance per watt. As a result, demanding CPU tasks such as editing images, compiling code, indexing new files, and running agentic AI workloads are faster than ever.
Accelerated GPU and Faster Memory Bandwidth
M6 features a 12-core GPU—two more cores than M5—with a Neural Accelerator in each core. This design delivers a nearly 30 percent increase in peak GPU compute for AI compared to M5, and more than 8x compared to M1, enabling significantly faster prompt processing when interacting with on-device LLMs.In addition, M6 offers Apple's latest advanced graphics capabilities, including updates to the shader core architecture, Dynamic Caching, and hardware-accelerated ray tracing. These technologies combine to deliver stunning visual realism, faster rendering, and higher frame rates for gaming. M6 also has 50 percent increased geometry rates for complex graphics.
M6 supports up to 32 GB of unified memory to multitask across demanding apps and run LLMs on device for secure and private agentic tasks. It also provides up to 170 GB/s of unified memory bandwidth—a 10 percent increase over M5 and a 2.5x increase over M1.M5 Ultra: The Ultimate Powerhouse for Pro Workflows
M5 Ultra, Apple's most powerful chip ever, is built for pros who need to speed through workloads that demand maximum CPU and GPU performance and unified memory bandwidth, such as complex 3D rendering, visual effects, scientific analysis, and running compute-intensive frontier AI models on device.
M5 Ultra uses UltraFusion to connect two dual-die M5 Max chips to form the quad-die architecture—a first for Apple silicon. UltraFusion increases the inter-die bandwidth to over 4.4 TB/s and the connection density by over 6x. Together, these ultra-low-latency, high-bandwidth interconnects allow the four dies to behave as a single unified processor. M5 Ultra also features a large up-to-36-core CPU consisting of 12 super cores and 24 performance cores, delivering up to 1.25x higher single-threaded performance and up to 1.3x higher multithreaded performance than M3 Ultra.
Unprecedented AI and Graphics, Massive Memory Capacity
M5 Ultra features a next-generation GPU with up to 80 cores, incorporating a Neural Accelerator in each core to offer up to 4.5x the peak GPU compute for AI compared to M3 Ultra and over 6x more than M1 Ultra. The GPU includes Apple's latest shader core with second-generation Dynamic Caching, as well as hardware-accelerated mesh shading and third-generation ray tracing, delivering up to 40 percent faster graphics performance than M3 Ultra.M5 Ultra incorporates a more capable Media Engine. Dedicated hardware-enabled H.264, HEVC, four ProRes encode and decode engines, and hardware-accelerated AV1 decode make it the ultimate solution for high-resolution video editing. M5 Ultra also includes a 32-core Neural Engine, driving complex AI tasks and Apple Intelligence features securely on device with industry-leading energy efficiency.Additionally, M5 Ultra features a massive amount of high-bandwidth unified memory, up to 512 GB, and delivers a staggering 1.2 TB/s of unified memory bandwidth that is 50 percent higher than M3 Ultra. This lets users store huge datasets entirely in local memory, increase the tokens-per-second speed, and run huge LLMs with hundreds of billions of parameters entirely on device.
Unleashing Power for Developers
Apple's developer frameworks and tools—including Core AI, Core ML, Metal, and Xcode—tap directly into the advanced hardware of both chips. Developers can leverage the Dual 16-core Neural Engine in M6, and the Neural Accelerators in the GPU with the massive 512 GB unified memory pool and faster 1.2 TB/s of unified memory bandwidth in M5 Ultra, to provide incredible AI compute capabilities.
With these frameworks and new chips, developers can run and fine-tune large AI models locally on their Mac. Apple's developer tools and frameworks automatically optimize performance across the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine, and give developers the ability to use Apple Foundation Models, App Intents to tap into Apple Intelligence features, or their own proprietary AI models to build and run powerful AI workloads entirely on device.

articles.title: 1 088 ch et 800 km d’autonomie : Tesla lance son plus grand véhicule électrique en Europe
articles.text:
Puisqu’une seconde génération des Model 3 et Model Y semble pour le moment hors de propos, Tesla tente de se développer autrement en Europe, en tentant une percée sur un marché pour le moins inattendu. Sa nouvelle star développe 1 088 ch, roule 800 km sans recharger et mesure plusieurs mètres de haut. Forcément, ce n’est pas une voiture, mais un camion, le fameux Semi qui sévit déjà aux États-Unis.
Son arrivée en Europe est extrêmement tardive, puisque la marque américaine a présenté son poids-lourd il y a maintenant neuf ans. Une éternité, qui a finalement laissé un peu de marge pour que les acteurs européens développent leur propre offre. Mercedes, Volvo, MAN, Scania et Renault ont aujourd’hui des modèles électriques, que ce soit des petits porteurs ou des grands routiers. Tesla arrive donc avec du retard, bien que le marché demeure embryonnaire.
Le grand bain des salons européens : simple show ou vraies commandes ?
Le Semi fera ainsi ses premiers pas sur le Vieux Continent à l’occasion du salon IAA Transportation Expo se tenant le 15 septembre à Hanovre, en Allemagne. L’engin y était déjà présent en 2024, mais uniquement sous forme de prototype. Cette fois-ci, il ne sera pas là juste pour le show, mais bien pour espérer donner l’eau à la bouche et engranger de futures commandes.
Pour ce faire, Tesla a assuré que le modèle présenté sera enfin finalisé en configuration européenne avec toutes les normes qui en découlent. Il était temps, car la production du Semi a bel et bien commencé à la Gigafactory du Nevada, où la marque entend fabriquer près de 50 000 modèles par an. Un bel objectif pour lequel l’Europe jouera un rôle clé ? Malgré des annonces qui se veulent naturellement rassurantes, des inconnues demeurent.
Déjà, le style si particulier du Semi devrait être affecté par quelques modifications mineures. C’est le cas des feux de gabarit orange situés en haut de la cabine propres aux modèles américains signalant des véhicules larges. Ces lumières n’existeront pas en Europe. L’aménagement intérieur avec son siège central si singulier pourrait subsister. En revanche, la plus grosse interrogation se situe au niveau de la recharge.
Le talon d’Achille de Tesla : un monstre impossible à recharger en Europe ?
800 km d’autonomie avec une puissance de charge pointant à 1 200 kW, c’est très bien pour abattre efficacement les kilomètres. Le problème, c’est que seuls les Megachargers peuvent délivrer un tel débit. Et ils n’existent pas encore en Europe. Se brancher sur les Superchargers est possible, mais pour la batterie de 822 kWh du Semi, cela deviendra de la charge lente type Destination Charger que l’on trouve sur les parkings d’hôtels.
Le poids-lourd, lui, a besoin de nettement plus de puissance. Il faudra donc soit se plier aux bornes rapides actuelles délivrant jusqu’à 600 kW ou attendre un éventuel déploiement des Megachargers en Europe. Bref, la route risque encore d’être particulièrement longue… Quant aux prix, ils demeurent inconnus, mais devront logiquement être bien placés car ils conditionneront le succès du véhicule.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (August 26, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: daily roundup (August 26, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Wednesday, August 26, 2026.
From Girl Rising’s battle against gender stereotypes using cricket to AssessPrep’s data-driven revolution in the classroom, YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Featured stories
Girl Rising’s RISE Premier League is using cricket to challenge gender stereotypes
On August 11, 2026, around 300 people gathered at the Government Higher Secondary School, Bhadi, in Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh, for something the village had never seen before—a cricket match in which girls and boys played together on the same team, as equals.
It was the opening match of the RISE Premier League (RPL) organised by non-profit Girl Rising as part of its flagship RISE education programme. The league features four mixed-gender teams and eight matches, and ends on October 10.
How AssessPrep is turning test scores into data schools can use
A test score tells a school how a student performed, but not necessarily where their understanding is strong or weak. AssessPrep, an assessment platform, tags every question to a topic and curriculum standard, allowing schools to see where an individual student or an entire class is falling short.
The platform, headquartered in Gurugram with operations in Jaipur, helps schools create, deliver, grade, and analyse tests, primarily for international curricula such as IB, Cambridge IGCSE, and Advanced Placement. It works with more than 800 schools, with an AI-first approach designed to save teachers time while giving schools more detailed data on student learning.
Latest news
Anaptyss bets on AI to drive value-led growth in BFSI
Anaptyss, the US-headquartered digital technology company with a significant presence in India, sees artificial intelligence (AI) as a key growth driver as it adds complementary capabilities to its existing portfolio of solutions.
Founded in 2021, Anaptyss has a strong focus on the banking, financial services and insurance (BFSI) sector, providing domain-led managed services to the industry. The company is now leveraging AI to expand its offerings and tap into new growth opportunities.
More than half of GCCs signal increased hiring in FY27: Report
The hiring outlook among global capability centres (GCCs) in India remains positive for FY27, although the focus is shifting towards hiring quality professionals rather than pursuing volume-led growth, according to a report.
The annual GCC survey by Taggd, in partnership with CII, titled From Intent to Predictable Scale: The Future of GCCs in India, found that 52% of GCCs plan to expand their workforce in FY27, up from 47% in the previous fiscal year.
Funding news
Emerald AI raises $150M at $1.05B valuation
Emerald AI, a US startup developing software that allows AI data centres to adjust their electricity consumption according to grid conditions, has raised $150 million in an oversubscribed Series A round at a valuation of $1.05 billion.
The financing was co-led by Energize Capital, an investment firm focused on the energy transition, and DCVC, a deeptech venture capital firm. The round also included strategic and financial investors such as NVIDIA, Samsung Ventures, Siemens, Aramco Ventures, Salesforce Ventures, GE Vernova, RWE, and JERA Ventures.
Ringg AI raises $10M in Series A led by Peak XV Partners
Bengaluru-headquartered voice artificial intelligence (AI) startup Ringg AI has raised $10 million as an extension to its Series A funding round, led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from Arkam Ventures and Capital 2b. The startup had earlier this year raised $5.5 million as part of its Series A round.
The startup, which is also backed by Kunal Shah, was founded in October 2023 by Siddharth Shankar Tripathi (formerly with Groww and Flipkart), Utkarsh Shukla (ex-Blinkit and Atlan), and Kali CV (ex-Flipkart).
Scooby’s Club raises $250,000 to expand dog care network
Bengaluru-based dog care company Scooby’s Club has raised $250,000 in a pre-seed funding round led by TDV Partners. Founded in 2025, the company operates neighbourhood dog daycare, boarding and spa facilities, combining free-roam spaces with canine behaviour-led care.
The funding will support the opening of two additional Bengaluru properties over the next 6 to 12 months, alongside hiring and training canine coaches. Scooby’s Club plans to eventually build a network of 100 properties across major Indian cities. The company said its facilities include temperament-based grouping, climate-controlled indoor spaces, personalised care and 24-hour CCTV access for pet owners.
Cüraa raises Rs 40 Cr in Series A funding
Kitchen and lifestyle brand Cüraa has raised Rs 40 crore in a Series A funding round led by 3one4 Capital, with continued participation from Kae Capital, Lumikai and Better Capital. The company will use the funding to expand its pre-cook and cooking product portfolio, strengthen warehousing and supply chains, expand across D2C, marketplaces and quick commerce, and hire senior leadership.
Founded by Chef Sanjyot Keer and Neeraj Kumawat, Cüraa has served more than 3 lakh households since launching in September 2024. The company says its monthly net revenue has grown 25-fold since launch, with an average product rating above 4.5 and an NPS exceeding 70.
Other news
Chola Foundation provides flood relief to 1,250 Assam families
The Chola Foundation, in partnership with Smile Foundation, has provided flood relief across 10 affected regions in Assam, supporting more than 1,250 families. The intervention focused on essential and hygiene needs, with dry rations, hygiene kits and other supplies distributed to affected households, particularly women, children, elderly people and people with disabilities.
The relief effort was coordinated with local authorities and community leaders to identify affected communities. Chola employees in Assam also volunteered in the distribution of supplies, following safety guidelines issued by district authorities.
Octave opens Hyderabad technology centre with plans to hire 2,000 engineers
Octave Intelligence has inaugurated a 2 lakh sq ft Technology and Innovation Centre in Hyderabad, with plans to scale its engineering workforce to 2,000 in the coming years. The centre will support Octave's global operations across software engineering, AI, data, cloud and product development. It also houses an Experience Centre showcasing the company's industrial intelligence and AI solutions.
The facility is located in HITEC City and will develop technologies for customers across asset-intensive industries, including energy, manufacturing, infrastructure, utilities and transportation. Octave serves around 4,500 customers across 180 countries, including more than 60% of the Global Fortune 500.
Qure.ai appoints Mihir Bhanushali to lead global health expansion
Qure.ai has appointed Mihir Bhanushali as Executive Vice President, Global Health, to lead its expansion across low- and middle-income countries. Bhanushali joins from Freshworks, where he was Senior Director, Global Sales, and has previously held leadership roles at Rippling and Whatfix.
He will oversee growth across Africa, Southeast Asia, South Asia and Latin America, covering infectious disease programmes and frontline care delivery. Qure.ai's AI solutions are deployed across more than 107 countries and 5,200 sites. The company is also expanding beyond screening and diagnosis through Aira, its AI doctor and clinical co-pilot for frontline healthcare.
Vodafone Business, Tech Mahindra partner on UK digital transformation
Vodafone Business has partnered with Tech Mahindra to develop digital transformation solutions for UK enterprises. The collaboration combines Vodafone Business' enterprise connectivity and digital infrastructure with Tech Mahindra's expertise in AI, systems integration, digital engineering and managed services.
The companies will explore industry-specific solutions using AI, automation, private 5G, IoT, cloud and data to modernise operations, improve resilience and support new business models. The agreement includes executive engagement, co-innovation and joint go-to-market activities, with both companies identifying opportunities to address customer requirements and deliver measurable business outcomes.
Quest Global joins Babcock engineering services framework
Quest Global Engineering Services has been appointed to Babcock International’s Engineering Services Framework under a five-year agreement, expanding an existing collaboration between the two companies that began in 2023. The engagement covers Babcock programmes across Nuclear, Marine, Aviation, Land and Mission Systems. The agreement is part of Babcock’s strategy to build closer, long-term partnerships with key suppliers.
Quest Global will draw on its multidisciplinary engineering capabilities, outcome-focused delivery model and international experience across complex programmes. The partnership is expected to create opportunities to support initiatives focused on scale, operational performance, affordability and long-term resilience. Quest Global will work with Babcock and its wider ecosystem on projects spanning multiple domains and geographies, strengthening the scope of its engagement with the international defence company.
Foresight Law Offices launches DPDP compliance desk
Foresight Law Offices has launched a dedicated Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Desk and an interactive DPDP Readiness Assessment Tool to help organisations prepare for India’s Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023. The initiative comes as businesses review their data practices ahead of the framework’s rollout. The DPDP Desk brings together the firm’s expertise across privacy, technology, cybersecurity, regulatory and corporate advisory.
Its services cover DPDP readiness, privacy and data governance frameworks, consent mechanisms, data principal rights, third-party data processing arrangements, data security and breach response. It also supports organisational policies and documentation while tracking regulatory developments. The interactive assessment tool provides organisations with an initial structured view of key considerations under the DPDP framework, helping them identify areas requiring attention as they prepare for compliance.
Client Associates appoints Siddharth Pardesi as chief business officer
Multi-family office and private wealth management firm Client Associates has appointed Siddharth Pardesi as Managing Partner and Chief Business Officer – HNI. Based in Mumbai, Pardesi will lead the company’s high-net-worth individual business as the firm builds on its position in wealth management. Pardesi brings more than two decades of experience across consumer banking, wealth management, investment products and advisory, as well as branch sales and distribution.
During his career, he has held senior roles at organisations including HSBC, BNP Paribas Sharekhan, Standard Chartered Bank and IndusInd Bank. His appointment is expected to strengthen Client Associates’ HNI business as it continues to engage with high-net-worth clients and expand its wealth management operations.
Embark named Major Contender in Everest Group assessment
Embark, an integrated service provider for Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in India, has been named a Major Contender in Everest Group’s 2026 PEAK Matrix Assessment of GCC Setup Capabilities in India. The assessment evaluates providers on their ability to help enterprises establish GCCs, based on Everest Group’s annual Request for Information process, provider briefings and client reference interviews.
The recognition highlights Embark’s focus on GCC setup and enablement. Its model combines consulting, talent solutions, workspaces and enabling services to support companies establishing GCCs in India. Everest Group’s assessment also highlighted Embark’s Workforce Ramp Planning Toolkit and GCC Incubation-to-Scale playbook. These capabilities provide clients with a structured approach to achieving operational readiness and scaling their GCC centres.
Manish Dalal appointed NEN president
The National Entrepreneurship Network (NEN) has appointed Manish Dalal as President as it expands its efforts to enable entrepreneurs and businesses across India. Dalal brings more than 25 years of experience in general management, business development and international expansion across AI, SaaS and cloud businesses in the US and APAC markets. He joins NEN after holding senior leadership roles at technology companies including Motorola, Yahoo, Verisign, Endurance and Nextiva.
As President, Dalal will lead NEN’s entrepreneurship portfolio, covering programmes such as Wadhwani Ignite, Wadhwani Liftoff, Wadhwani Accelerate and WadhwaniEntrepreneur.ai. His responsibilities will also include Wadhwani FPO Entrepreneurship and Wadhwani SHG Micropreneurship. He will lead Wadhwani Government AI Platforms, which uses AI to support government programmes and improve livelihoods.
CureMeAbroad receives medical travel certification
CureMeAbroad, the medical tourism discovery and patient-navigation platform operated by Luxora Health Care Experiences, has received Medical Travel Facilitator Certification from Global Healthcare Accreditation (GHA). The certification strengthens the platform’s focus on safety, transparency and quality across the international patient journey. CureMeAbroad is now among a select group of medical travel facilitators globally certified under GHA’s programme for organisations that coordinate international patients with healthcare providers.
Unlike hospital accreditation, the certification evaluates organisations operating between patients and healthcare providers. It assesses leadership and accountability, patient services, risk management, business ethics, cultural and language support, staff training, financial and marketing transparency, and data protection. The certification comes as international patients increasingly rely on facilitators to navigate healthcare systems, compare treatment options and coordinate travel and post-treatment requirements.
Tribe Kombucha partners with Wow! Momo
Mountaintribe Foods, the maker of homegrown probiotic beverage Tribe Kombucha, has entered into a distribution partnership with Wow! Momo, one of India’s largest quick-service restaurant chains. Under the partnership, Tribe Kombucha will be made available across Wow! Momo’s network of more than 900 stores in over 100 cities across India. The company is scaling its distribution network as it prepares for its next phase of growth.
Blackbaud opens second Hyderabad office
Blackbaud, a provider of AI-powered solutions for social impact, has opened its second office in Hyderabad as it expands its operations in India. Located in the Financial District, the new facility is expected to support customers, product development initiatives and global operations while providing capacity for the company’s next phase of growth in India. Blackbaud expects its India workforce to continue expanding as it invests in future-ready talent and capabilities, including AI and cloud technologies.
Its existing HITEC City office houses Product Management, Enterprise Technology, Data Engineering and Research and Development teams. The new office will primarily support Blackbaud’s expanding Customer Operations organisation. Together, the two Hyderabad offices will support technology, customer and business functions, reinforcing India’s role as a collaborative delivery and support hub within Blackbaud’s global operating model.
Cashfree Payments launches AI agent Relay
Cashfree Payments has launched Relay, an AI-powered Super Agent designed to automate payment operations for small and medium-sized businesses and startups. Relay, which has been in beta with merchants since May 2026, is now available to all Cashfree merchants. According to Cashfree, seven in 10 Indian SMBs handle payment operations entirely manually, while most of the remainder use tools covering only a single channel or workflow.
Relay can execute tasks including retrying failed payments, following up on abandoned carts, confirming cash-on-delivery orders before dispatch, managing failed subscriptions and filing disputes ahead of deadlines. Cashfree said an average SMB spends 60 hours a week on payment operations, while Relay aims to reduce this to less than 45 minutes. The platform operates entirely on Cashfree infrastructure, with merchant transaction data not sent to external AI providers.
Fynd expands digital commerce platform for Woodland
AI-native retail technology company Fynd is powering the next phase of omnichannel growth for outdoor footwear and apparel brand Woodland by extending its unified Order Management System (OMS) and Warehouse Management System (WMS) across Woodland’s 171 stores and central warehouse operations. The integration is designed to improve inventory visibility, fulfilment agility and digital commerce operations. Woodland has integrated its store network and central warehouse operations on Fynd’s platform, creating a unified ecosystem across channels.
Fynd’s OMS enables omnichannel fulfilment and real-time inventory synchronisation across marketplaces including Myntra, AJIO, Flipkart, Nykaa, Nykaa Fashion and Tata Cliq. The connected platform integrates stores, warehouse, ERP, POS systems and digital channels. During peak sales periods, Woodland’s stores fulfil up to 2,500 orders daily, while the warehouse processes up to 2,000, creating a combined peak load of 4,500 orders.
Coverfox appoints Shikha Gupta as Chief Strategy Officer
Technology-led insurance distribution platform Coverfox has appointed Shikha Gupta as Chief Strategy Officer, effective July 1, 2026. Gupta will work with the leadership team to drive strategic growth, strengthen corporate partnerships and support Coverfox’s expansion across Bharat. She brings more than 18 years of experience spanning global finance, investing, financial services and portfolio leadership. Her areas of expertise include corporate strategy, capital allocation, mergers and acquisitions, governance and financial services.
Before joining Coverfox, Gupta served as Investment Director at Elevar Equity, where she evaluated investment opportunities across financial services, MSME lending, consumer businesses and insurance. Her appointment comes as Coverfox focuses on strategic growth and broader expansion. Gupta’s experience across investing and financial services is expected to support the company’s corporate partnerships and strategic initiatives.
Aziro launches enterprise AI agent platform Aziron
Aziro has launched Aziron, an enterprise agent execution platform designed to help organisations move beyond AI-generated answers and complete governed work. The platform brings agents, workflows, documents, models and enterprise tools together within a single governed environment. Aziron includes purpose-built modules for technical and business teams. Pulse focuses on engineering workflow automation, Atlas provides local-first code intelligence, Signal supports AIOps and incident reasoning, Canvas enables data apps and dashboards, while Harness provides model routing and cost control.
The platform is designed around governance, traceability and auditability. Aziron is now available as a self-hosted platform for on-premises deployment or customer-managed cloud environments. It also supports local models for private deployments, enabling organisations to retain greater control over their enterprise AI environments and data while using agents to execute business and technical workflows.
Matrix Geo Solutions completes 314-km highway survey
Geospatial technology and engineering consultancy Matrix Geo Solutions has completed a highway survey covering approximately 314 km across five road sections under LOT-2/HARYANA/Package-1. RITES Limited awarded the project on behalf of the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).
The assignment formed part of consultancy services for preparing a Detailed Project Report for economic corridors, inter-corridor and feeder routes aimed at improving freight movement efficiency in India. Matrix Geo Solutions was responsible for mapping physical, utility and land-related characteristics across the identified highway sections.
(This article will be updated with the latest news throughout the day.)

articles.title: Cisco expands rack-scale secure AI factory infrastructure for neocloud and sovereign clouds - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cisco expands rack-scale secure AI factory infrastructure for neocloud and sovereign clouds
Cisco Systems Inc. today introduced an expansion to its current lineup of rack-scale artificial intelligence solutions for massive AI workloads in secure AI factories, addressing growing needs for massive inference and training compute.
Through a partnership with Super Micro Computer Inc., Cisco announced an expanded portfolio of Secure AI Factory solutions with Nvidia Cloud Partner-compliant solutions for hyperscale, neocloud and sovereign clouds. It features the company’s Silicon One-based switches for the front end and builds on the company’s Nvidia Spectrum-X-based switches on the back end, unified by Nexus One, Cisco’s networking management platform.
“We are at the beginning of one of the largest datacenter buildouts in history,” President and Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel said. “Every organization is racing to scale AI — but speed only counts if it comes with control of data, managed token costs and real return on investment.”
The company said it has also expanded its Enterprise Reference Architectures to include the latest generation for enterprise deployments. This will allow small deployments and large datacenter projects to rapidly spin up and prototype networking and rack-scale build-outs using Nvidia AI deployments with very little risk by tapping into well-known expertise and best practices.
As is already fundamental to large-scale AI factories and high-throughput compute, liquid cooling dovetails nicely with Cisco’s hardware. Modern rack-scale systems, such as Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72, can exceed 200 kilowatts per rack – the company said its Cisco N9000 Series Switches are liquid-cooled and interoperate with Supermicro rack-scale, liquid-cooled compute to deliver rack-to-fabric speeds at AI factory throughput.
As the race to bring trillion-parameter training and high-throughput inference use cases to the enterprise burns bright, heat exchange will remain a major data center bottleneck. Platforms including the aforementioned NVL72 and Nvidia HGX Rubin NVL8 will continue to work at the front lines, requiring combined cooling systems alongside networking.
“With Cisco Secure AI Factory with Nvidia, we no longer have to choose between performance, reliability or ease of management,” said James Manning, co-founder and Chief Executive of Sharon AI. “NCP validation gives us the confidence that our infrastructure is optimized from day one.”
By combining effort between Cisco and Supermicro, the partnership offers solutions for compute and networking infrastructure that are pressure-tested for service-ready enterprise environments. The company added that, once delivered, new Cisco Validated Services will help customers certify infrastructure to make certain it is built, designed, and aligned to reference architecture.
This way, datacenter compute, networking, security and resilience retain the standards and best practices outlined in deployment guidelines.
During operations, Nvidia AI Enterprise software and AgentOps delivered through the Cisco Cloud Control backend will allow customers to use their own tooling and utilities. The company said it expects this will allow most customers to enjoy using the hardware and software delivered by an AI Factory as if it were a robust expansion, instead of a complete overhaul.
“The AI Factory is a new concept – generating tokens and generating revenue. But that AI Factory needs to sit within your existing enterprise infrastructure,” Mark Hamilton, Nvidia’s vice president of solution architecture and engineering, said in an exclusive interview on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. “The lifeblood of AI is data. When you go use ChatGPT or Gemini, those are great models, but they are trained on public data. Cisco networking has access to enterprise data that is not accessible on the internet.”
Hamilton added that it’s more than just a rack-scale solution, providing factory-wide access for graphics processing units to vast amounts of data. That connectivity could open compute and networking for hundreds of thousands of GPUs at scale to handle the traffic volume for the AI inference needed in the agentic AI era.
The Supermicro compute solutions will roll out as part of the Cisco Secure AI Factory with Nvidia beginning October this year.

articles.title: KI im Studium: Neue Studie zeigt beliebteste KI für Hausarbeiten – und es ist nicht ChatGPT
articles.text:
KI im Studium: Dieser Chatbot hat beim akademischen Schreiben die Nase vorn
In den USA verwenden College-Student:innen ChatGPT häufiger als jede andere Nutzungsgruppe. Das ging im vergangenen Jahr aus einem Bericht des Anbieters OpenAI hervor. Aber liefert der Chatbot wirklich die besten Antworten für akademische Texte wie Hausarbeiten oder Essays? Laut einer Analyse der Plattform Studyarena gehört ChatGPT bei Student:innen zwar zu den drei beliebtesten Tools, schneidet im Blindtest aber am schlechtesten ab. Stattdessen führt Gemini von Google das Ranking an. Für die Analyse wurden im August 2026 insgesamt 6.851 anonyme Stimmen ausgewertet.
Mehr Reasoning ist nicht unbedingt besser
Studyarena führte unter Student:innen einen Blindtest mit Antworten von ChatGPT, Claude und Gemini durch. Sie sahen die Antworten und wählten jene aus, die ihnen am besten gefielen – ohne den Namen des Modells zu kennen. So sollte verhindert werden, dass persönliche Meinungen die Auswahl verfälschen. Das Ergebnis: Bei Schreibaufgaben belegte Gemini mit einer Auswahlquote von 39,6 Prozent den ersten Platz. Claude erreichte 31,8 Prozent und ChatGPT 29,2 Prozent.
Laut Studyarena kam es bei den KI-generierten Antworten vor allem auf die Ausgewogenheit an. „An der Hochschule wird selten ein einzelnes Extrem belohnt. Die beste Antwort ist vollständig, ohne formlos zu wirken, sie ist strukturiert, ohne mechanisch zu klingen, und sie ist klar, ohne die Stimme der Verfasser:innen zu verwässern“, heißt es in der Auswertung.
Laut der Untersuchung bevorzugten Student:innen tendenziell längere Texte. Die ausgewählte Antwort war im Durchschnitt 37 Prozent länger als die Alternativen. Die längste Antwort gewann 47,7 Prozent der entscheidenden Vergleiche, die kürzeste immerhin 25,0 Prozent. Interessant ist, dass längere Gedankengänge der KI nicht zwangsläufig zu beliebteren Antworten führten – die Analyse zeigte sogar das Gegenteil. Antworten mit niedrigem Reasoning erzielten mit 40,7 Prozent die höchste Zustimmung, während Antworten mit längeren Argumentationsprozessen nur 29,5 Prozent erreichten. Eine mögliche Erklärung ist, dass längeres Nachdenken zu mehr Wiederholungen führen könnte, was sich negativ auf den Schreibstil auswirkt.
Eine klare Empfehlung für Textaufgaben
Die Autor:innen der Studyarena-Analyse empfehlen Student:innen, beim Schreiben von Hausarbeiten oder Essays zunächst eine normale oder niedrige Reasoning-Stufe zu wählen. Diese sollte nur erhöht werden, wenn es um das Argumentieren anhand von Belegen geht, nicht für das Schreiben selbst. Gemini erzielte zwar die beste Gesamtwertung für akademisches Schreiben, sei aber nicht das einzige hilfreiche Tool. ChatGPT liefere laut Analyse bei der Recherche das beste Ergebnis und Claude bei der Aufgabenplanung. Wer nur ein Abonnement abschließen möchte, dem rät Studyarena dennoch am ehesten zu Gemini.
Auch in Deutschland ist die Nutzung von KI unter Student:innen weit verbreitet. Laut einer Umfrage der Hochschule Darmstadt gaben im vergangenen Jahr knapp 92 Prozent von ihnen an, entsprechende Tools im Studium einzusetzen. Das war ein deutlicher Anstieg gegenüber der ersten Erhebung von 2023, als die Quote noch bei 63 Prozent lag. Demnach kommen KI-Tools am häufigsten zum Klären von Verständnisfragen zum Einsatz: Mehr als zwei Drittel nannten diesen Verwendungszweck. Weitere 52 Prozent nutzen KI-Tools zur Analyse, Verarbeitung oder Erstellung von Texten. An der Studie beteiligten sich 4.910 Student:innen aus 395 Hochschulen.
Die Online-Abstimmung läuft weiter
Student:innen können bei Studyarena weiterhin für ihre bevorzugten Antworten abstimmen, sodass sich das Ranking mit der Zeit noch ändern könnte. Die Ergebnisse sind jederzeit live einsehbar und decken auch andere Studienfächer wie Mathematik, Medizin und Philosophie ab. Je nach Einsatzbereich liegen auch hier unterschiedliche Anbieter vorne. Das unterstreicht einmal mehr, dass sich für verschiedene Fächer und Aufgaben unterschiedliche Modelle lohnen können.

articles.title: Qué son las llaves de acceso de WhatsApp y cómo activarlas para proteger tu información
articles.text:
WhatsApp continúa implementando medidas que prevengan la vulneración de las cuentas. Por ello, recientemente incorporó la posibilidad de registrar múltiples llaves de acceso en una misma cuenta, una función que refuerza la protección de los usuarios y simplifica el ingreso a la aplicación desde distintos dispositivos.
La medida se enmarca en una serie de actualizaciones de seguridad impulsadas por Meta, la empresa propietaria de la plataforma.
Las llaves de acceso —conocidas en inglés como passkeys— son un método de autenticación moderno que elimina la necesidad de recordar y escribir contraseñas tradicionales. En lugar de una combinación de letras y números, el sistema utiliza los mecanismos de seguridad integrados en el propio dispositivo del usuario para verificar su identidad.
PUBLICIDAD
Dentro de WhatsApp, esto se traduce en el uso de datos biométricos como la huella dactilar, el reconocimiento facial (Face ID) o el código de bloqueo de pantalla. La verificación biométrica reduce el riesgo de acceso no autorizado y elimina la dependencia de claves que podrían ser interceptadas o adivinadas.
Más de mil millones de personas ya tienen configurada esta función en sus dispositivos. Ahora, la plataforma admite más de una llave por cuenta, lo que facilita la gestión cuando se alternan equipos con sistemas operativos distintos, tanto Android como iOS.
PUBLICIDAD
Cómo activar las llaves de acceso
El proceso de configuración es directo y no requiere conocimientos técnicos:
- Abrir WhatsApp e ingresar a Ajustes
- Seleccionar la sección Cuenta
- Tocar la opción Llaves de acceso
- Desde ese menú, registrar los métodos de desbloqueo disponibles en cada dispositivo
Una vez completado el registro, el usuario podrá iniciar sesión sin contraseña, con una verificación más rápida y sin los riesgos asociados a los códigos PIN tradicionales.
PUBLICIDAD
Identificación de llamadas desconocidas
Otra de las novedades implementadas por WhatsApp apunta a mejorar la seguridad en las llamadas recibidas desde números que no figuran en la agenda del usuario. En dispositivos Android, la aplicación ahora despliega información adicional sobre el origen de cada llamada, como el país del número y si existe algún grupo compartido entre ambos contactos.
La función está diseñada para dar tiempo y contexto antes de contestar, lo que permite al usuario evaluar la legitimidad del contacto. Los estafadores suelen apelar a la urgencia para obtener una respuesta inmediata; esta herramienta busca contrarrestar esa táctica al poner más datos a disposición del receptor antes de que tome una decisión.
PUBLICIDAD
Verificación en dos pasos con contraseñas más robustas
La verificación en dos pasos también recibió una actualización. El método, que hasta ahora exigía un PIN de seis dígitos, permite desde la última versión establecer una contraseña de mayor longitud que puede incluir caracteres especiales y letras, lo que eleva el nivel de protección de la cuenta.
Para modificar esta configuración, los pasos son los siguientes:
- Ingresar a Ajustes dentro de WhatsApp
- Seleccionar Cuenta
- Tocar Verificación en dos pasos
- Reemplazar la clave actual por una combinación alfanumérica
WhatsApp recomienda evitar secuencias básicas como “123456” y optar por claves difíciles de predecir, en línea con las prácticas estándar de seguridad digital. Si la clave activa es una combinación simple, la plataforma sugiere cambiarla de inmediato.
PUBLICIDAD
Todas estas funciones operan en paralelo con el cifrado de extremo a extremo, una característica que, según WhatsApp, garantiza que las conversaciones permanezcan únicamente entre el remitente y el destinatario, sin posibilidad de acceso por parte de terceros.
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: Melhor notebook para estudar: o que avaliar antes da compra • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Resumo
- O tipo de uso define as especificações do notebook; para uso básico, como navegação e pacote Office, configurações intermediárias atendem bem.
- As especificações técnicas, como processador, memória RAM, GPU e armazenamento, definem o desempenho do notebook.
- O Dell 14, Dell 2 em 1 Inspiron 14 e Dell 15 são opções de notebooks que oferecem bom desempenho, tela e portabilidade para estudos.
Escolher um notebook para estudar muitas vezes começa por uma pergunta simples: para que ele será usado? Por isso, a compra não deve partir apenas do preço ou de características físicas, como tamanho e peso, mas também de especificações como processador e bateria.
Um aparelho errado pode causar travamentos durante pesquisas, incompatibilidade com plataformas e ter que lidar com um equipamento obsoleto antes mesmo da formatura. Para que o investimento valha a pena, a decisão precisa ser baseada nas exigências reais da sua rotina. Entenda o que considerar ao comprar um novo notebook para estudos.
O que avaliar antes de comprar um notebook para estudos
Vale entender o tipo de uso: aulas por vídeo, trabalhos em texto, planilhas, apresentações, leitura, programação, edição de vídeos ou outros softwares específicos do curso. Alguns pontos já ajudam a filtrar a escolha:
- Desempenho: processador, memória RAM e armazenamento definem a fluidez do sistema.
- Tela: tamanho, resolução e conforto visual pesam em longos períodos de leitura.
- Bateria: importante para quem estuda fora de casa ou passa o dia entre aulas.
- Portabilidade: notebooks menores são mais fáceis de levar na mochila.
- Conexões: portas USB, HDMI, entrada para fone e leitor de cartão evitam depender de adaptadores.
- Formato de uso: um modelo 2 em 1 pode ser útil para leitura, anotações e apresentações.
Uso e compatibilidade
O tipo de curso deve orientar a configuração. Para navegação, pacote Office, PDFs e outras plataformas básicas, um notebook com configurações intermediárias já pode atender bem. Entretanto, programação, edição de imagem e vídeo e modelagem 3D, por exemplo, exigem mais poder de processamento e gráfico.
Especificações técnicas
Após entender o tipo de uso, vale olhar para alguns pontos principais: processador, memória RAM, GPU e armazenamento. Eles que definem como o notebook vai lidar bem com multitarefa, arquivos pesados e os programas acessados.
- Processador: define a capacidade do notebook para lidar com tarefas simultâneas e programas. Linhas como Intel Core 3/Core i3 atendem usos diários, como navegador, edição de texto e aulas online. Para tarefas que demandam mais processamento, vale priorizar processadores com mais núcleos e maior fôlego, como configurações das linhas Intel Core 5/Core i5 ou Core 7/Core i7.
- Gráficos: GPUs integradas atendem bem ao uso acadêmico comum, incluindo videochamadas, reprodução de mídia e tarefas de edição.
- Memória RAM: ajuda o notebook a manter vários programas e abas abertos ao mesmo tempo. 8 GB podem atender uma rotina básica de estudos, enquanto 16 GB oferecem mais fôlego para multitarefa.
- Armazenamento: o SSD deve ser prioridade, porque deixa a inicialização do sistema, a abertura e gravação de arquivos mais rápidas. 256 GB podem funcionar para quem usa bastante serviços de nuvem, mas opções a partir de 512 GB são ideais pois permitem instalar mais programas e salvar arquivos sem depender tanto de armazenamento externo.
Tela e construção
Como estudar no computador envolve passar horas lendo e digitando, o conforto também precisa entrar na decisão.
- Tela: modelos de 14 polegadas favorecem mobilidade e cabem melhor na mochila. Já modelos com telas maiores oferecem mais espaço para multitarefas e reprodução de mídia. Em qualquer tamanho, vale priorizar resolução Full HD, acabamento antirreflexo e recursos de conforto visual, como redução de luz azul.
- Teclado e touchpad: teclas bem espaçadas ajudam a reduzir erros em trabalhos longos. Para cursos de exatas, o teclado numérico pode agilizar cálculos e planilhas. O touchpad precisa ter boa resposta para facilitar o uso em sala de aula, biblioteca ou deslocamentos.
- Formato 2 em 1: pode fazer sentido para quem lê muitos textos, faz anotações, apresenta trabalhos ou prefere alternar entre notebook e tablet. É um formato mais flexível, especialmente para aulas e estudos fora da mesa.
Bateria de longa duração
A bateria é uma parte extremamente importante nessa equação. O ideal é buscar aparelhos capazes de entregar pelo menos cerca de oito horas de uso real.
Considere, também, o carregamento: modelos como o Dell 14 e o Dell 15 contam com ExpressCharge, recurso que permite recarregar até 80% da bateria em 60 minutos.
Outro ponto é a eficiência do sistema e da construção. Dispositivos com boa distribuição de calor e recursos para ajustar energia e temperatura conforme o uso ajudam a manter o desempenho mais estável ao longo do dia.
Conectividade e webcam
Um notebook com boas conexões evita que o estudante dependa de adaptadores para tarefas simples, como conectar um pendrive, usar fones de ouvido, projetar uma apresentação ou transferir arquivos de um cartão SD.
Entre as conexões mais úteis estão:
- USB-A: para pendrives, mouse, teclado e acessórios comuns.
- USB-C: para transferência de dados e, em alguns modelos, vídeo ou alimentação.
- HDMI: para monitores, TVs e projetores.
- Entrada para fone de ouvido: útil em aulas online e chamadas.
- Leitor de cartão SD: facilita a transferência de fotos, vídeos e outros arquivos.
Já a qualidade da webcam e do microfone influenciará diretamente em aulas remotas, reuniões em grupo e apresentações online. Considere dispositivos com webcam HD e recursos de redução de ruído no microfone.
Melhores notebooks para estudo
Dell 14
O Dell 14 é um modelo de 14 polegadas, com 1,56 kg de peso e um formato mais fácil de transportar, ideal para quem precisa levar o aparelho para aulas e trabalho.
A tela chega à resolução 2,5K, com brilho de 300 nits, o que ajuda na leitura e videochamadas. O notebook também traz webcam FHD com redução de ruído temporal, áudio Dolby Atmos.
Pode ser encontrado em versões de 8 GB a 32 GB de RAM DDR5 e 512 GB a 1 TB de armazenamento, com processadores Intel Core 5 120U ou Intel Core 7 150U.
Conheça todos os detalhes do Dell 14 no site da Dell.
Dell 2 em 1 Inspiron 14
O Dell 2 em 1 Inspiron 14 é uma opção para quem quer alternar entre notebook e tablet. O formato é útil para rotinas de muita leitura, revisão de textos e anotações, já que permite usar o mesmo aparelho em diferentes posições.
O dispositivo tem opções de 8 GB a 16 GB de memória RAM DDR5, com 512 GB ou 1 TB de armazenamento.
Veja as especificações do Dell 2 em 1 Inspiron 14.
Dell 15
O Dell 15 é a alternativa para quem prefere uma tela maior e teclado mais completo. A tela Full HD de 15,6 polegadas tem acabamento antirreflexo, e o ComfortView ajuda a reduzir a emissão de luz azul em usos prolongados.
O modelo também traz teclado espaçoso, teclado numérico separado e atalho para calculadora, recursos úteis para planilhas, cálculos e trabalhos longos.
Nas configurações disponíveis, o Dell 15 pode vir com processadores Intel Core i5 e Core i7, além de memória DDR5 de até 16 GB e SSD de 512 GB ou 1 TB.
Saiba mais sobre o Dell 15 no site da Dell.

articles.title: Google's anti-nausea Motion Assist dots finally rolling out on Android
articles.text:
Some people are cursed with motion sickness, which can make it impossible to read or use a phone in a moving vehicle without suffering waves of nausea. There’s a surprisingly simple trick that can make smartphones usable in such situations. Apple deployed it on the iPhone a couple of years ago, and now Google’s own version is finally coming (slowly) to Android.
Motion sickness is caused by a disagreement between what your inner ear senses and what your eyes see. If you’re looking at a book or a screen while in a car, the sensory mismatch can lead to a pretty unpleasant time. As part of iOS 18 in 2024, Apple released a feature called Motion Cues that places a network of moving dots on the screen to alleviate motion sickness, and it seems to work surprisingly well. Google’s version is similar, but it’s called Motion Assist.
Google began testing Motion Assist back in 2024, but it never expanded beyond an internal test until now. Android Authority reports Motion Assist is appearing on Pixel phones running Android 17, but there’s no app or update you can install to get the feature—it’s being delivered by Play Services as part of a staged rollout.
When activated, Motion Assist adds small dots around the edges of your phone screen over top of the content. It plugs into your phone’s accelerometer and gyroscope, allowing the dots to move in concert with the motion of the vehicle; they travel down the screen while the vehicle is moving forward, to the left when turning right, and so on. They basically mimic the way objects in the real world would move through your vision if you weren’t glued to the screen. Here’s how Apple’s version works.

articles.title: Will you be buying a plug-in solar kit? The tech becomes legal in the UK on August 27 — have you say in our poll
articles.text:
Plug-in solar kits become legal in the UK tomorrow — but will you be buying one?
The big day is almost here — and now we want to hear from you
- Plug-in solar kits become legal in the UK from August 27
- These lower-cost solar panels are ideal for renters and flat owners
- We want to hear from you in our poll below — will you be buying one?
Plug-in solar kits become legal in the UK from August 27, which makes that date a pretty significant one in the UK's energy history.
That's because these kits are, in theory, a much more affordable and user-friendly way to bring the bill-cutting benefits of solar power to your home. The UK government estimates that plug-in panels could save households up to £70-£110 a year on their energy bills.
For renters and flat owners with little roof space, they represent a long-awaited new alternative to pricey rooftop installations. Instead, as their name suggests, you can theoretically plug them directly into your mains electricity, and place them outdoors in places like balcony railings, fences, garden sheds or patios.
However, despite their promised savings, early plug-in solar kits aren't exactly cheap. Early options that have gained regulatory approval, such as the UKSOL Plug-In Solar Pro Compact 460W Ground Mount Kit, will start at £699 from retailers, and it isn't yet clear when we'll be able to buy them directly from the likes of Lidl, Amazon and Currys.
Other potential drawbacks include limitations on where you can actually install plug-in solar (in some cases, you may need planning permission) and the fact that you can't currently connect your panels to a battery, without professional help. For many, plug-in batteries are the real game-changer, and some will be waiting for those to become legal before diving into plug-in solar.
But now we want to hear from you — are you planning to buy a plug-in solar kit when they become legal on August 27? Vote in our poll below and let us know your thoughts in the comments too.

articles.title: One gigabyte of RAM cost as much as a house back in 1995 — $64,000 price tag resurfaced in 31-year-old press release, equivalent to $140,000 today
articles.text:
One gigabyte of RAM cost as much as a house back in 1995 — $64,000 price tag resurfaced in 31-year-old press release, equivalent to $140,000 today
By the looks of it, we're going back to that pricing, too.
Looking back in time is always interesting, especially when visiting any topic that's technology-adjacent — and doubly so when looking at the evolution of pricing. The price of memory continues to be a hot-button topic, and an eagle-eyed Redditor came across a 1995 press release from Advantage Memory Corporation announcing prices for its freshly released DIMMs, revealing that fitting a high-end machine with 1 GB of RAM would set you back as much as a cheap house.
The figures on display are rather shocking when converted to today's dollars, with 8 MB of RAM going for $399, or $874 in today's money, and a 64 MB stick ringing in at $3,900, or $8,540 in 2026. The Apple Power Macintosh mentioned in the PR had 12 slots, so it could fit in as much as 1.5 GB of RAM, and although the pricing for 128 MB DIMMs wasn't mentioned, those would be around $8,000 a pop, so "only" 1 GB of RAM would come in at $64,000 — enough for a house back then in the more affordable areas of the U.S. By the way, that amount would be $140,000 today.
In 1995, memory technology was transitioning from SIMMs to the spankin' new DIMMs, and Command and Conquer, MechWarrior 2, and the original Need for Speed were coming out. 16 MB of RAM was generally accepted as a decent amount of memory for a build, roughly matching the 16 GB of today. Some quick math says those 16 MB of the new technology were about $800, or in today's money, the princely sum of $1,751.
As of today, 16 GB of DDR5 will set you back $200 to $250, but the price of memory has been extremely volatile, to say the least. Plus, not only is supply rumored to drop, server RAM contract prices are expected to rise, and the few crumbs left for the consumer market are still rising in price.
SK hynix chairman Chey Tae-won even suggested that DRAM wafer shortages could last until 2030 at least. The fact that all the major RAM makers are shifting their production lines to HBM for AI accelerators is only making the problem worse. Yes, $200 is still a long way from $1,750, but with things keeping in this direction, there's a non-zero chance this very article will be linked to in the near future.
At any rate, despite the poor outlook, these figures reveal just how much technology really became democratized with time. Any form of PC was really expensive back in 1995. Around that era, Bill Gates said that there would be "a PC at every home, and at every desk." That statement sounded a little insane back then, but in retrospect wasn't crazy enough, as today we have what would be sci-fi hardware... in everyone's pocket or purse.
